newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends mixed in rangebound trade.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends mixed in rangebound trade.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL

PALM OIL FUTURES - The market ended mixed in another rangebound trading day with a lack of participation seen dampening sentiment. Price movements were still locked in a tight range on a lack of fresh leads. June futures will still traded in the 1,230 and 1,250 range.
PALM PHYSICAL - Little dealing interest was seen and prices were barely changed amid uncertainty in fundamentals.
The June futures contract ended at 1,239 ringgit ($494.22), one ringgit higher than Monday's close.
The June futures contract is still consolidating in this range with uncertainty in fundamentals also seen dampening sentiment, traders said.
News that Malaysia's palm oil stocks are expected to total around 700,000 tonnes at end-June 1997 against 774,000 tonnes at end-June 1996 had no impact on the market, traders said.
"Sentiment turned easier as some profit-taking emerged towards the morning close," a trader said, adding that players were also cautious amid uncertainty in the market outlook.
Traders said the market appeared to be consolidating with third month, June futures expected to trade between 1,230 and 1,250 ringgit.
The market had risen earlier due to gains in Chicago soyoil futures overnight which prompted some short covering and speculative buying, traders said.
The market was expected to move in a boxed-range in the near-term, unless some fresh leads appear. Uncertainty in the fundamental outlook also limited price movements, they said.
Turnover on the futures market was 1,404 lots.
